# Cinder

> Cinder is a semantic runtime for websites you control. Tag real routes, actions,
> fields, and outputs with plain HTML attributes (cinder-route, cinder-action, etc.),
> and Cinder resolves text or voice commands against that structure entirely in the
> browser, before ever reaching an AI model.

Cinder runs in three tiers: a deterministic local graph (Tier 1, free, in-browser),
a client-side embedding model for typo/paraphrase recovery (Tier 2, free, in-browser),
and an optional AI fallback for genuinely open-ended requests (Tier 3, paid, via
Cinder Relay) that only runs when the first two tiers cannot resolve a command.
Most user commands never leave the browser and never call an AI model.

Install: `npm install usecinder`

## Docs

- [Get started](https://usecinder.dev/get-started): installation and first integration
- [Documentation](https://usecinder.dev/docs): full reference for routes, actions, fields, and tiers
- [Agent setup prompt](https://usecinder.dev/get-started/prompt.md): a copy-paste prompt for coding agents to integrate Cinder automatically
- [Blog](https://usecinder.dev/blog): design rationale and updates
- [Cinder Relay](https://usecinder.dev/docs/relay): the hosted AI-fallback billing product (Tier 3)

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/harry-sandhu/usecinder): source code, license (Elastic License 2.0), issues, and discussions
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/usecinder)
